edges.reason: offering_ is used directly as the mint destination in the initial supply distribution.
public_ is used directly as the mint destination in the initial supply distribution.
team_ is used directly as the mint destination in the initial supply distribution.
fund_ is used directly as the mint destination in the initial supply distribution.
mine_ is used directly as the mint destination in the initial supply distribution.
liquidity_ is used directly as the mint destination in the initial supply distribution.
__MATTER_init calls __MATTER_init_unchained to perform the distribution.
_token is assigned to the token state variable inside start().
_recipient is assigned to the recipient state variable inside start().
_begin is assigned to the begin state variable inside start().
_span is assigned to the span state variable inside start().
_times is assigned to the times state variable inside start().
The governance modifier restricts who may configure token, recipient and the vesting schedule in start().
total is initialised from token.balanceOf(address(this)) inside start().
token.balanceOf(address(this)) is read when computing the unlocked amount.
total is multiplied by times.sub(i).div(times) in the unlock computation.
times is used in the loop bound and in the vesting arithmetic.
span is multiplied by i and divided by times in the unlock computation.
begin is added to the schedule offset in the unlock computation.
The loop counter i feeds the vesting step arithmetic.
block.timestamp (now) determines the branch taken in the vesting arithmetic, making the unlock amount timestamp dependent.
The SafeMath result computed in the arithmetic block is returned as the unlockCapacity() value.
unlockCapacity() branches on now (< begin and now < span*i/times + begin), so its result depends on block.timestamp.
unlock() uses the value returned by unlockCapacity() as the transfer amount.
The token state variable is the target contract of the safeTransfer call.
The recipient state variable is the destination of the safeTransfer call.
unlock() indirectly depends on block.timestamp through unlockCapacity(), so the paid-out amount is timestamp dependent.
unlock() performs an external token transfer to recipient before any state is settled, exposing a reentrancy surface via malicious token/recipient behaviour.
The fallback function silently invokes unlock(), so any plain ETH/value-less call can trigger the token transfer.
